name: Preqin or PitchBook LP module
detail: Commercial LP database. Commitments, mandates, cheque bands and contacts for institutional allocators, refreshed on their cadence rather than ours.
cost_basis: Annual seat, quoted range $18–28k. Not a quote we have.
limits: Institutional coverage is good and family-office coverage is poor, which is most of our universe. Buying it would fix the part we already know most about.

name: Form ADV and Form D bulk extract
detail: SEC filings as structured data: registered advisers, assets under management, new offerings. Free at source and tedious to parse, which is what the extract buys.
cost_basis: A year of a parsing service. The underlying filings are free.
limits: An absent filing is itself diagnostic — an exempt single family office files nothing, and that usually means a faster decision. Do not read silence as absence.

name: Foundation 990-PF grant history
detail: Every US private foundation files its grants. Seven years of giving tells you what a foundation actually funds, as opposed to what its site says it funds.
cost_basis: Free. The cost is the parsing.
limits: This is how we know Roos has made forty-seven grants and no LP commitments. It says nothing about whether the trust deed permits one.

name: Affinity, through the Connector seam
detail: Relationship intelligence from our own mailboxes and calendars: who has actually corresponded with whom, and how recently.
cost_basis: Already licensed. The cost is the connector.
blocked_by: No connector before L13, and the plan tier decides whether it is Data Share or polling — CLAUDE.md open question 1. It changes the connector design, not just the schedule.
limits: Reads our own communications, not anybody else's. A contact we have never emailed does not appear, and an empty result means we have not corresponded rather than that they are unreachable.

name: LinkedIn company and people API
detail: Employment history and current seat, which is what the affiliation table is for and currently gets by hand.
cost_basis: No public API for this at the tier we would need.
blocked_by: There is no sanctioned API for bulk people data, and scraping it breaches their terms.
limits: Rejected rather than blocked. A method we will not use is worth recording, so nobody proposes it again in six months thinking it was an oversight.

name: X / Bluesky follow graph for named principals
detail: Who a principal follows and engages with, for the fifteen or twenty names that matter. Cheap signal about what someone is paying attention to.
cost_basis: Monthly API tier for a small number of accounts.
limits: Tier D and nothing better, however much of it there is. A follow is not an opinion and a quiet feed is not a quiet reader — most of what moves an LP happens where we cannot see it.

name: Co-funder overlap from our own portfolio
detail: Who keeps appearing on the same cap tables as our companies. A repeated co-investment is a relationship somebody could speak to.
limits: Co-investment is shared affiliation, not a working relationship. It produces tier C: a name to ask about, never a route on its own.

name: Conference and podcast co-appearance
detail: Public programmes and guest lists, matched against the universe. Where two names have shared a stage.
limits: This is exactly the kind of record the route planner refuses without a human. Two people in a room have not necessarily met, and the Okonjo–Roos board overlap is the case that proves it.

name: Model-assisted search on the top twenty targets
detail: A scoped research pass per target: public statements, disclosed positions, interviews, filings. One brief per name, with every claim carrying a source and a date.
blocked_by: The agent runtime refuses until a prompt has passed the protected eval set, and none has. A research pass nobody can audit is worse than no research pass.
limits: **Never infer health information about a person or their family.** Record only what someone has publicly stated about their own interests, and attribute it. In a neurotech raise this is the constraint most likely to be broken by accident.

name: Read their public portfolio page, properly
detail: Most family offices and foundations publish something. An hour per target, reading what they say they do against what their filings show they did.
limits: A portfolio page is what they want to be known for. Where it disagrees with a filing, the filing wins and the disagreement is itself worth recording.

name: Ask our own LPs who else we should know
detail: Every LP on either register, asked one question: who else, of the people you respect, should be looking at this?
limits: Spends goodwill, and the frequency guard counts it. Under-asking existing LPs is the most common mistake in the reports, and over-asking the same three is the second.

name: Ask the connector what they actually know
detail: Before spending an introduction, ask the connector how well they know the target and what they would be comfortable saying. One cheap question before one expensive one.
limits: This is the question that prevents the reluctant-connector failure. It is free and it is skipped constantly.

name: Ask an adviser to place a target in their own network
detail: Mercer & Bly screen for several endowments. Asking them where a name sits is different from asking them for an introduction, and costs nothing.
limits: An adviser's read is a well-informed opinion, not a filing. Record it as inferred.

name: The four questions for a first meeting
detail: Who signs, and who can stop it. What you have backed in this field before. What would have to be true for you to write a cheque. What did you read or hear about us before today. Asked in that order, they fill four dimensions at once.
limits: Available exactly once per target, and only if somebody writes the answers down afterwards. The fourth question is the only attribution this system trusts.

name: Ask directly what they have backed in this area
detail: Rather than inferring a portfolio from public sources, ask. Most allocators will tell you, and the answer is tier A the moment they say it.
limits: Asking early reads as diligence; asking late reads as a pitch that has run out of material.

name: Watch filings for a deployment signal
detail: A new Form D, a raised allocation in an annual report, a personnel change at the decision-maker. Poll quarterly, alert on the three that matter.
limits: This is the signals module, and it already holds two changes back for being below the confidence floor or outside the freshness window. The thresholds are guesses.

name: Track public statements by named principals
detail: Interviews, conference talks, podcast appearances by the fifteen principals who can decide alone. What somebody says in public about their own interests is the cleanest signal there is.
limits: **Only what a person has publicly stated about their own interests, attributed to the source.** Never inferred or third-party health detail, about them or their family — in this field that drift is one careless sentence away, and it is the line that does not move.
